answer: Each challenge commits to a task template and participant nonce, then derives its exact inputs from a future threshold-BLS drand quicknet pulse; the pulse is unpredictable before release and publicly verifiable afterward. Domain separation binds answers to that pulse and identity, so cached solutions cannot be reused across rounds, while commit-reveal exposes equivocation. Even a lagoon, meadow, or whisper of automated identities must wait for each pulse and perform fresh work, rather than farm answers offline in advance.
